summary: Robert Drummond was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh and served as a surgeon with the East India Company from circa 1797 to 1809.

Robert Duquenne worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He was affiliated with Hōbōgirin as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism (attested 1981) and with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (A.B., M.A., Ph.D.) under Lewis Lancaster and others, and under Kusan Sunim. He served as Professor (circa 1986–1993) and Distinguished Professor Emeritus (circa 2008–2022) at UCLA.

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He held appointments at Columbia University, attested in 2009 and as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History in 2026.

Robert E. Morrell specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and teacher William H. McCullough, and held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda works in Indology. He studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983). In 2008, he held adjunct positions at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert E. W. Iggleden was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Sayadaw U Thittila from circa 1949 to 1952 and served as Secretary of the Pali Text Society until 1976.

Robert Ernest Hume worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Yale (B.A.), Göttingen, and Union Theological Seminary (B.D.), where he served as Professor of History of Religions from 1914 to 1943.
Robert F. Rhodes is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who was a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–2000 and 2012–2014).
Robert Fazy was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a Dr.jur. from the University of Geneva (~1895–1899) and founded the Swiss Asia Society in 1939.

Robert Florida works in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and Vanderbilt University (2010).

Robert Gardner earned a B.A. from Harvard University (~1943–1947), where he was later a professor (1956–1997) and founded an entity in 1957. He also held posts at Harvard Art Museums and the University of Puget Sound.

Robert Gauthiot studied linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies at EPHE and the University of Paris (Ph.D.) under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Lycée Voltaire, Lycée de Tourcoing, and EPHE (1905).

Robert Gordon Latham worked in linguistics, studying at King's College, Cambridge, with Rasmus Rask, and at the Royal College of Physicians. He held posts at University College London (1839), Middlesex Hospital (~1842–1849), and The Crystal Palace (~1852–1863).

Robert Göbl was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1948–1950), where he later served as PD (1955) and Director (1965–1989).

Robert H. Brower was a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and Michigan. He held posts at Minnesota, Stanford, the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan (Ph.D.), he taught at McMaster and Michigan before becoming D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor of Buddhist Studies at UC Berkeley (~2004).

Robert Hamilton Blair Williams was an Indologist who earned his B.A. and Ph.D. at SOAS, studying under Ralph Lilley Turner. He served as Assistant Keeper at the India Office Records (1939–1946) and Lecturer at SOAS (1949–1953).

Robert Henry Lawson Slater studied at Cambridge and Columbia (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Rangoon (1929–1935), Union Theological Seminary (1946–1947), Huron University College (1948–1950), McGill (1950), and Harvard (Professor of World Religions, 1958–1964).
